# NET-001: A host firewall is active and denies incoming traffic by default

- **Group:** Firewall and exposure
- **Severity when it fails:** high
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check reports `unknown`, never a pass.

## Why it matters

Without a default deny, every service that listens on a wildcard address is reachable by anyone who can route to the host. stackward accepts UFW (active, default incoming deny or reject), a running firewalld, an nftables input chain that drops by default, or an iptables INPUT policy of DROP. Without root only the UFW configuration files can be read; they say what loads at boot, not what is loaded, so the result stays unknown.

## Verify by hand

```sh
sudo ufw status verbose; sudo nft list ruleset; sudo iptables -S INPUT
```

## How to fix it

Allow SSH first (ufw allow in on tailscale0 to any port 22, or from one source), then: ufw default deny incoming; ufw enable

## What a fix can break

Enabling a default deny before allowing SSH locks you out; keep the provider console at hand. Services reached directly on the host stop answering until allowed.

Run `stackward explain NET-001` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
